subject.title: ACP parent session stuck until refresh when yielded waiting for child completion

question: Should OpenClaw define one heartbeat-independent yielded-parent wake contract across ACP and native subagents, or continue landing only narrow runtime-specific mitigations?
rationale: The source evidence shows partial fixes and open narrow PRs, but the complete behavior crosses runtime ownership, task terminal policy, heartbeat wake semantics, and channel delivery expectations.

options.title: Define One Core Wake Contract
options.body: Treat this issue as the canonical contract and require candidate PRs to compose into heartbeat-independent parent continuation across ACP and native subagents.

options.title: Land Narrow Slices
options.body: Accept the current open PRs as incremental mitigations while leaving broader ACP/native edge cases tracked separately.

options.title: Document Current Limits
options.body: Decline Phase B-style yield semantics for now and document heartbeat, announce, and best-effort delivery limits as current behavior.

recommendation.title: Define One Core Wake Contract
recommendation.body: Treat this issue as the canonical contract and require candidate PRs to compose into heartbeat-independent parent continuation across ACP and native subagents.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history shows broad work across the subagent cleanup, announce, and delivery paths where this product/ownership decision has to land.
